links.comparator_used: Domain-specialized MedGemma 27B (no external guideline retrieval) compared with general-purpose Gemini 2.5 (guideline-integrated)
links.outcome: Concordance with MTB decisions and clinical safety rate in 300 CRC cases
links.effect: Gemini 2.5: κ = 0.792, exact concordance 85.0%, safety 83.7%. MedGemma: κ = 0.566 (T=0.0) and 0.610 (T=1.0), accuracy 70.3% and 73.5%, safety 62.3% and 62.7%; p < 0.001 for the difference.
links.tradeoff: The comparison is confounded: Gemini had guideline integration and MedGemma had none, which the authors call a predefined asymmetry in knowledge augmentation. Discordance clustered in complex scenarios such as surgical planning, recurrent disease and poor performance status.
links.quote: A guideline-integrated general-purpose LLM demonstrated superior concordance and safety compared with a domain-specialized model operating without external retrieval, supporting its adjunctive use within MTBs while preserving expert clinical judgment.

links.comparator_used: MedGemma 27B operating without external guideline retrieval
links.outcome: Concordance with MTB decisions and clinical safety rate
links.effect: Guideline-integrated Gemini 2.5: κ = 0.792, 85.0% exact concordance, 83.7% safety. MedGemma without retrieval: κ = 0.566-0.610, accuracy 70.3-73.5%, safety 62.3-62.7%; p < 0.001.
links.tradeoff: Retrieval was not isolated. The arms differ in both model and guideline access, so the effect cannot be attributed to retrieval alone.
links.quote: A guideline-integrated general-purpose LLM demonstrated superior concordance and safety compared with a domain-specialized model operating without external retrieval, supporting its adjunctive use within MTBs while preserving expert clinical judgment.

links.outcome: Concordance with MTB decisions (kappa, accuracy) and safety rate
links.effect: T=0.0: κ = 0.566, accuracy 70.3%, safety 62.3%. T=1.0: κ = 0.610, accuracy 73.5%, safety 62.7%. Concordance improvement p = 0.038.
links.tradeoff: The improvement at T=1.0 was modest, and safety remained low at both settings.
links.quote: MedGemma showed moderate agreement at T = 0.0 (κ = 0.566; accuracy = 70.3%) and modest improvement at T = 1.0 (κ = 0.610; accuracy = 73.5%; p = 0.038), with lower safety rates (62.3% and 62.7%; p < 0.001).
